study type: Secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial
exposure: antenatal lifestyle intervention (low-glycaemic index diet and physical activity)
energy-adjusted dietary inflammatory index (E-DII™) in early and late pregnancy
cohort: The study included 434 mother-child pairs from the PEARS trial in Dublin, Ireland, consisting of women with overweight and obesity.
finding: The antenatal low-glycaemic index intervention significantly reduced the dietary inflammatory index (E-DII™) in pregnant women, although early pregnancy E-DII™ showed limited associations with most maternal and child outcomes, with the exception of an increased odds of adverse cardiometabolic phenotype in women delivering male infants.
mod_finding: No association was found between early pregnancy E-DII™ and mode of delivery.
cross-section timing: E-DII™ scores were calculated for early (10-16 weeks) and late (28 weeks) pregnancy.
